name: Cold Water Cove Campground
note: Willamette NF campground on the SE shore of Clear Lake (turquoise spring-fed lake; no power boats), at the end of FR770; 34 sites, no hookups, drinking water, vault toilets. RVs 18-50 ft depending on site. Both reservable and FCFS sites. --Claude

name: Sixes River Campground
note: BLM Coos Bay District (Myrtlewood FO) campground along the Sixes River E of the coast at Sixes; 19 sites, gravel spurs fit rigs up to ~30 ft, vault toilets, no potable water, no hookups; popular for salmon fishing and gold panning; first-come, first-served by self-registration; open Fri before Memorial Day-Sept 30. --Claude

name: Fairview Campground
note: Small 5-site drive-through loop off State Hwy 207 S of Spray, Umatilla NF (Heppner RD); accessible vault toilet, potable water fountain May-Oct; trailhead for 80 mi of OHV routes, used mainly by hunters; FCFS, maintained Memorial Day-mid-Nov. --Claude

name: North Fork John Day Campground
note: Umatilla NF (North Fork John Day RD) campground at the Blue Mtn summit on Hwy 52/73, along the Wild & Scenic North Fork John Day River at the wilderness trailhead; 20 sites (14 tent/RV, 5 tent-only, 1 group), ~15 fit RVs (site 2 pull-through), vault toilets, no hookups; some sites reservable on recreation.gov, rest FCFS. --Claude

name: Skull Hollow Campground
note: USFS Crooked River National Grassland (Ochoco NF) high-desert campground east of Terrebonne, popular Smith Rock State Park basecamp. ~28-70 large flat gravel sites incl pull-throughs and double sites, no hookups, pit toilets, no potable water; dry camping. First-come, first-served, cash/check pay envelopes. Most sites fit large RVs. --Claude

name: Blackberry Campground
note: USFS Siuslaw NF campground on a wooded bluff over the Alsea River, ~18 mi east of Waldport on Hwy 34. 32-33 sites with paved spurs, picnic tables, fire rings; no hookups, no dump station. On-site boat ramp (drift boating, salmon/steelhead). First-come, first-served per recreation.gov. --Claude

name: Ash Flat Campground
note: USFS Umpqua NF (Tiller RD) primitive campground near the South Umpqua River, open year-round. 4 shaded sites with tables and fire pits, vault toilet, no potable water, no hookups. Max vehicle length 35 ft. First-come, first-served with pay envelopes. --Claude

name: South Umpqua Falls Campground
note: USFS Umpqua NF (Tiller RD) open-meadow campground near South Umpqua Falls, ~20 mi up County Rd 46 from Tiller. ~20 sites for tents/trailers/RVs, vault toilets, no potable water, no hookups. First-come, first-served via recreation.gov Scan & Pay. --Claude

name: Threehorn Campground
note: USFS Umpqua NF (Tiller RD) campground near the Rogue-Umpqua Divide on the scenic road between Tiller and Trail, ~2,600 ft. 5 sites shaded by pine and fir, tables and fire pits, vault toilet, no potable water, no hookups. Max vehicle length 22 ft (borderline for a 23-ft rig). First-come, first-served with pay envelopes. --Claude

name: Packard Creek Campground
note: USFS (Willamette NF, Middle Fork RD) campground on the west side of Hills Creek Reservoir SE of Oakridge. 36 standard sites for RV/trailer/tent (14 reservable, rest first-come), plus a group area; day-use with swim area, fishing dock and boat ramp. Reservable on recreation.gov and FCFS. --Claude

name: Woodward Campground
note: Umatilla NF (Walla Walla Ranger District), ~20 mi E of Weston on Hwy 204 near Tollgate; paved highway access. About 14-18 standard nonelectric sites, max RV/trailer 25 ft, vault toilets, dump station on site, no hookups. Some sites reservable online, others first-come, first-served. Small pond/marsh beside the loop. --Claude

name: Sam Brown Campground
note: Rogue River-Siskiyou NF (Wild Rivers Ranger District), Briggs Valley SW of Grants Pass; centered on a historic meadow. About 19 standard nonelectric sites, max vehicle length ~24 ft, vault toilets, no potable water, no hookups. First-come, first-served (cashless scan-and-pay via Recreation.gov app). Access is via a narrow, winding, steep forest road (FR 2500/2512) - fine for a compact 23-ft rig but not large RVs. Separate Sam Brown Horse Camp is nearby. --Claude

name: Dovre Recreation Site
note: BLM Northwest Oregon District (NOT Oregon Dept. of Forestry) on the Nestucca River National Back Country Byway along the Nestucca Wild & Scenic River, W of Willamina. About 10 sites plus a group shelter, paved parking pads, picnic tables/fire rings, two vault toilets, seasonal potable water, no hookups. Reservable online or first-come, first-served with on-site payment; season ~May-Sept, no cell reception in the drainage. --Claude

name: Lower South Fork Campground
note: Rogue River-Siskiyou NF (High Cascades Ranger District) on the South Fork Rogue River, ~8 mi up FR 34 from the Butte Falls/Prospect area; gravel forest-road access. About 6 sites in old-growth forest, picnic tables/fire pits, vault toilet, no potable water, no hookups; small forest sites ('not big-rig friendly') that suit a compact 23-ft rig, comparable South Fork-area sites cap ~24-25 ft. First-come, first-served, seasonal (adjacent South Fork Campground is temporarily closed). --Claude

name: Port of Arlington Marina RV Park
note: Port of Arlington (port district) RV park on the Columbia River at the John Day pool; ~12 sites with full hookups (water/electric/sewer) plus an upper dry-camping area nearer the water; boat launch, dump station, showers. FCFS / call to reserve. --Claude

name: Willow Point County Campground (Howard Prairie Lake)
note: Jackson County park on Howard Prairie Lake in the Cascades (elev ~4,600 ft), east of Ashland; 41 campsites, no hookups; boat ramp and fish-cleaning station. Open May-Oct; reservable online/by phone or FCFS. --Claude

name: Harney County Fairgrounds RV Park
note: Harney County fairgrounds RV park at Burns; 30 full-hookup pull-through sites (30/50-amp), open year-round 24/7 for public camping (NOT event-only; sites held only for the annual fair and major rodeos). First-come first-served, self-pay fee box. --Claude

name: Willow Lake County Park
note: Jackson County park on Willow Lake below Mt. McLoughlin (7.5 mi east of Butte Falls); 63 sites - 19 full-hookup, 12 water/electric, 32 no-hookup - plus cabins and yurts; store, showers, dump, boat ramp. Concessionaire-run ("Willow Lake Resort") on county land. Reservable, FCFS within 14 days. --Claude

name: Armitage Park
note: Lane County park on the McKenzie River ~5 mi north of Eugene; 37 full-hookup (water/electric/sewer/cable/WiFi) RV/tent sites, open year-round, reservable (Lane County's portal sells single nights; checked for a July 2027 weeknight, 2026-10-12). Boat ramp, off-leash dog park, day-use areas. --Claude

name: Sunnyside County Park
note: Linn County park on Foster Reservoir off Quartzville Rd, ~3 mi off Hwy 20. 130 water/electric hookup sites plus 35 non-hookup sites; 42 sites kept first-come, first-served, rest reservable online. Boat ramp, fish-cleaning station, two stocked ponds. Open early April to early November; big-rig accessible. --Claude

name: Whitehorse County Park
note: Josephine County park ~8 mi west of Grants Pass along the Rogue River with a bird sanctuary and river-access trails. 5 full-hookup RV sites (30 amp) plus 9 tent sites and 1 yurt; reservations required. RV Life unrated (0 reviews) but a confirmed operating county campground. --Claude

name: Cantrall Buckley Park
note: Jackson County park on the Applegate River (~1.75 mi frontage) near Ruch, 8 mi W of Jacksonville. 30 basic no-hookup sites (+1 group camp), flush restrooms with showers; sites take RVs/trailers though some are tight with narrow roads for larger rigs. First-come, first-served, no reservations, open ~Apr 10-Oct 5. --Claude

name: Morgan Lake Campground
note: City of La Grande primitive campground on Morgan Lake atop the hill ~2 mi (steep ~17% grade) SW of La Grande; grade is manageable by smaller RVs and travel trailers. ~13 lakeside sites with tables and fire rings, no hookups, no drinking water. First-come, first-served, 3-night limit; open ~Apr 22-Oct 31 (gate closes 10pm). --Claude

name: Boice Cope Park
note: Curry County park on the shore of Floras Lake, ~14 mi north of Port Orford off US-101. 31 sites: 18 paved RV spaces with water/electric hookups, 13 tent sites; restrooms, showers, dump station. Reservable online; unreserved sites available FCFS for 1 night. Popular with windsurfers/kiteboarders. --Claude

name: Waterloo County Park
note: Linn County park on the South Santiam River, ~5 mi east of Lebanon off Hwy 20; 128 acres with over a mile of river frontage. 120 sites, 100 with water/electric hookups and concrete pads. Loop A (109 sites) reservable, Loop B (11 sites) first-come first-served in summer. Restrooms, showers, dump station, disc golf. --Claude

name: John Neal Memorial Park
note: Linn County park bordering the North Santiam River at Lyons, 30 acres, open April-September. 24 individual sites plus a 12-site group area; 10 RV sites with water hookups (no electric/sewer) and pull-through availability, rest are rustic tent sites. Flush toilets, showers. Reservations required (no FCFS). --Claude

name: Toll Bridge Park
note: Hood River County park on the East Fork Hood River near Parkdale, open ~May 1-Oct 31; 60 sites with electric & water (of 81 total; 21 tent-only), flush toilets, hot showers, dump station. First-come, first-served -- reservations not accepted. --Claude

name: Hewitt / Holcomb County Park
note: Baker County park on the Powder River arm of Brownlee Reservoir near Richland; combined Hewitt & John Holcomb parks, ~48 RV/tent sites with paved boat ramps, fish-cleaning stations and a dump station. Open mid-March through Oct 31 with limited FCFS dry camping Nov-Feb. --Claude

name: Hunt Park (Wasco County Fairgrounds)
note: Wasco County-operated campground at the county fairgrounds in Tygh Valley, at the base of Mt. Hood near the Deschutes. ~120 sites with power and water (shared dump station), big-rig friendly, restrooms and showers, tent areas. General camping available; self-registration (envelope drop box), no reservations for RV/tent sites. Camping is genuine year-round, not event-only. --Claude

name: Windy Cove County Park - Campground A
note: Douglas County park on Salmon Harbor Dr at Winchester Bay, facing Salmon Harbor at the mouth of the Umpqua River. Loop A has 29 sites (1-25 full hookup, 26-29 electric), RVs to 60 ft; reservable up to 11 months out ($10 fee), some FCFS. Walking distance to the village, crab dock and dunes. --Claude

name: Windy Cove County Park - Campground B
note: Douglas County park on Salmon Harbor Dr at Winchester Bay, between a mature Sitka spruce stand and Salmon Harbor. Loop B has 69 sites (1-40 full hookup, 41-69 no-hookup) plus 2 cabins, RVs to 60 ft; showers, playground, crab dock and boat launch access. Reservable up to 11 months out, some FCFS. --Claude

name: Emigrant Lake - The Point RV Park
note: Jackson County park on a point at the north end of Emigrant Lake, minutes from Ashland. 32 full-hookup sites (water/50-amp/sewer), 14x50 ft pads for larger RVs, picnic tables/fire rings, flush restrooms/showers; open year-round, FCFS with reservations recommended. --Claude

name: Quosatana Campground
note: Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest (Gold Beach RD) campground on the Wild & Scenic Lower Rogue River, ~14 mi up County Rd 595 / FR-33 from Gold Beach. 43 drive-in sites (3 ADA) spread over a 15-acre river bar, RVs to 30 ft, flush toilets, drinking water, dump station, boat launch. First-come, first-served (no reservations; cashless Scan-and-Pay via recreation.gov as of 7/2026). --Claude

name: Bird Track Springs Campground
note: Wallowa-Whitman NF campground in the Grande Ronde River valley off Hwy 244, ~14 mi W of La Grande (I-84 exit 252). 22 wooded sites under ponderosa pines, vault toilets, no drinking water/hookups; reviewers report easy backing for larger rigs. Reservable on recreation.gov with some FCFS. Interpretive trail along the river across the road. --Claude

name: Merrill Mobile Manor & RV Park
note: Small-town RV park in Merrill (Klamath Basin) combined with a manufactured-home section; 32 spaces total, 23 full-hookup back-ins plus 6 non-metered big-rig pull-thrus, 50-amp, coin laundry/showers. Takes nightly transient RVs first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Magone Lake Campground
note: USFS Malheur National Forest campground on Magone Lake in the Blue Mountains (Blue Mountain RD). ~21 pull-through individual sites, no hookups, vault toilets, drinking water (summer only); RVs/trailers up to 30 ft. Individual family sites first-come, first-served (only the group site/pavilion is reservable on recreation.gov). One RV per site. Federal (USFS), not commercial despite RV Life tag. --Claude

name: Scaponia Park
note: Columbia County park along the East Fork Nehalem River, 10 mi east of Vernonia on the Scappoose-Vernonia Hwy. Small primitive campground (~12 sites), first-come, first-served; drinking water, restrooms, picnic tables, fire pits, no hookups. Open drive-in gravel/grass area fits small rigs; county orients it to tent camping so best for tents and small RVs. --Claude

name: Kershaw-Ryan State Park
note: Canyon campground: 16 units total; 12 developed sites with 30/50-amp electric + water hookups (reservable), plus 4 FCFS tent-only sites; restroom, coin showers, RV dump station. Reservable via ReserveNevada. --Claude

name: Lahontan State Recreation Area
note: Nevada State Parks recreation area on 17-mi-long Lahontan Reservoir (Reclamation dam, state-park operated). Camping is largely drive-on beach/shoreline camping at the numerous developed beaches (Silver Springs Beach, Beach 7, Churchill Beach) plus some defined sites; vault toilets, dump station, no hookups. Reservable online for some areas; much of the shoreline is first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: South Fork State Recreation Area
note: Nevada State Recreation Area on South Fork Reservoir south of Elko. 25-site campground off the north park access road with tables, grills and a flush restroom with showers; no hookups but East Campground has powersites and a year-round RV dump station is near the north entrance. Reservable online plus FCFS; 14-day/30-day limit. --Claude
